conflict_synopsis.core_view: CA-US 2Y at -140bp is a policy-path-and-energy dislocation, not a fair two-speed gap, and should converge as Canada’s front end re-rates versus a US 2Y that already sits next to 2028 SOFR.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: BoC path reprice off CORRA Dec 2.58 as energy pass-through and global tightening catch up with a post-FOMC CA-US 2Y overshoot.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: CA-US 2Y through the 2025-01-30 analog of -145bp with CORRA Dec still near 2.58, or Canada core/labor remaining too soft for any catch-up.

paper_capital.rationale: Funded seat pays 5.00% ACT/365 on the full $100m whether flat or not, so remaining in cash still burns vig. $10m (10% of allocation) on a positive-carry RV — receive US 2Y 4.76 versus pay CA 2Y 3.27, about 149bp of yield advantage — plus expected spread convergence from a 5y 4th-percentile gap is the size that can beat staying flat without using a fabricated mark. No executable broker prices in the packet; if the book engine cannot represent CA-US 2Y, the parent should record execution_blocked/HOLD rather than invent a fill.

remit: historical or fundamental dislocations and convergence trades
stance_summary: Narratives that Canada is a durable low-rate peer versus a hiking Fed are cheap. The tradeable object is the CA-US 2Y yield spread at -140bp, a 1y and 5y historical left-tail, after a post-FOMC cheapening that a >90% priced hike cannot explain. Valuation anchor is the policy-path-normalized 2Y differential plus energy terms-of-trade/pass-through, not the percentile itself. Convergence should begin now because CORRA still prices only +29bp through December while US 2Y already sits close to 2028 SOFR, BoC minutes flag energy pass-through, and global tightening broadened after the Fed move.

catalysts: Next BoC communications/data that lift the CORRA strip off 2.58 toward the 69bp already sitting in CA 2Y versus Dec CORRA.
Energy pass-through into Canadian headline/core that validates the minutes.
Global tightening confirmation (further BoJ/BoE/Fed path firmness) that forces Canada to re-rate rather than remain the low-rate residual.
Mean-reversion of the 5d z -2.17 cheapening if it was a post-FOMC flow residue rather than a new BoC easing impulse.

context_build.causal_mechanism: Verified fact: Fed funds is 3.75–4.00% after a 25bp hike, SOFR 3.85, with ICE 1M SOFR implying 4.1975 by Dec-2026 and 4.6025 by Aug-2028; CORRA 2.29 with MX futures implying only 2.58 by Dec-2026; Canada August CPI held at 3% with core near 2%; BoC minutes flag higher energy pass-through; retained energy research treats CAD terms-of-trade and an inflation/rates tail as live. Inference: a two-speed policy cycle is real, but the sovereign 2Y gap has cheapened as a residual of the US-led selloff rather than as a fair-value BoC path. The mechanism being tested is that energy pass-through plus broader global tightening force Canada’s front end to re-rate higher versus a US 2Y that already embeds most of the observable SOFR path, so CA-US 2Y converges from historically depressed levels. Unknown: CORRA path beyond Dec-2026 (only four contracts).

Same 1m-move analog 2024-12-18: level -130bp, then 1m -3bp, 3m -20bp — cheapness persisted.

Same 1m-move analog 2024-05-02: level -63bp, then 1m -9bp, 3m -6bp. The 2025-01-30 episode is the only analog at a comparable depressed level; its 3m outcome was +25bp of spread widening (less negative).
historical_reference.distribution: CA-US 2Y as of 2026-09-17: -140bp, 1y percentile 3.77, 5y percentile 4.31, z_1y -1.84, z_5y -1.51. Packet 252-day window: percentile 3.57, z -1.86. CA-US 10Y: -111bp, 1y percentile 0.20, 5y percentile 10.60. These are left-tail levels, not merely a down-week.
historical_reference.regime_differences: 2025-01-30 was not a week-after-Fed-hike tape with BoJ at a 31-year high and an explicit BoC energy pass-through flag. Today’s US 2Y 4.76 is already near Aug-2028 SOFR 4.60, whereas several 2022 analogs were early-cycle (US 2Y 2.13 on 2022-03-23 then +59bp/+88bp forward). Canada’s labor gauge is 38 versus US 75 and core inflation is near 2%, which can justify a wide gap and is the main reason this is not a blind percentile fade. CORRA visibility ends at Dec-2026 versus a SOFR chain to 2028. Saudi ship-to-ship crude via Oman reduced the extreme oil-supply tail, so the energy-inflation catalyst is live but not unbounded. NZ rates are unavailable and are not used.

independent_checks: Policy-path check versus sovereign 2Y: SOFR 3.85 → Dec 4.1975 (+35bp) → Aug-2028 4.6025 (+75bp) versus CORRA 2.29 → Dec 2.58 (+29bp). US 2Y is 16bp above 2028 SOFR; CA-US 2Y still -140bp. Two datasets (overnight benchmarks plus listed STIR) versus official 2Y yields.

Macro triangulation: US inflation/labor/activity/consumer gauges 72/75/69/74 versus CA 55/38/66/45; Canada August CPI 3% headline / core near 2% versus August US CPI keeping Fed tightening intact. Hotter US justifies some gap; it does not uniquely justify a 4th-percentile 5y 2Y spread after a priced hike.

Cross-market: CA-US 10Y also at a 1y floor (-111bp, 0.2nd percentile) so the cheapness is not a 2Y quirk. USDCAD versus CA-US 2Y r-squared 0.022 (weak) — FX is not independently confirming, which is why the rates RV owns the discrepancy.
Positioning: US 2Y AM nets 12.5th percentile 1y; CAD leveraged net still short but 99th percentile 1y of net with weekly covering. Ownership does not explain a new fundamental cheapening.
context_build.known_vs_new_information: Known before the 5d cheapening: Reuters 2026-09-16 that rate futures entered FOMC with >90% odds of 25bp; August US CPI had already kept Fed tightening bias intact; Canada August CPI 3%/core near 2% was printed 2026-09-14. New or newly transmitting: the hike was delivered (3.75–4.00%); BoJ hiked 25bp to 1.25% (31-year high, 7–2); 18 Sep desk thesis that global tightening is broadening and the energy shock is constraining easing even where growth is softer; BoC minutes flag energy pass-through into that global-tightening tape. A known, almost fully priced Fed hike cannot by itself explain CA-US 2Y then cheapening another 15bp in 5d (z -2.17) while CORRA still only prices +29bp through December.
context_build.market_assumption_disagreed_with: Disagreement is not that the US is hotter than Canada (labor 75 vs 38, inflation gauges 72 vs 55 — that gap is real). Disagreement is that CORRA +29bp through December is a sufficient Canada path once energy pass-through is a BoC-flagged risk, energy shock absorbers are weakening, and global tightening has broadened, while US 2Y already sits next to the 2028 SOFR terminal. The priced assumption that is wrong: CA-US 2Y at -140bp is fair value of a settled two-speed cycle rather than a lagging residual that should start converging now.
context_build.market_implied_assumption: Priced in SOFR/CORRA: the Fed has hiked and will average SOFR near 4.20 by December and 4.60 by Aug-2028; BoC stays near 2.29–2.58 through year-end. Priced in sovereign 2s: US 2Y 4.76 is only about 16bp above Aug-2028 SOFR 4.6025 and 56bp above Dec SOFR 4.1975; CA 2Y 3.27 is about 98bp above CORRA 2.29 and 69bp above Dec CORRA 2.58, but that still leaves CA-US 2Y at -140bp, inside the 4th percentile of the last five years. The market’s assumption is that the two-speed cycle is durable: Canada remains a structurally lower-rate peer and the 140bp 2Y gap does not need to close on a 1–3 month horizon.
context_build.path_to_current_price: Verified fact: CA-US 2Y is -140bp as of 2026-09-17 (1d -1bp, 5d -15bp, 1m -17bp, 3m -9bp, 6m -46bp, 1y -43bp). US 2Y 4.76 is 99.8th percentile 1y / 88th percentile 5y; CA 2Y 3.27 is 97.8th percentile 1y / 58.6th percentile 5y. CA-US 10Y is even cheaper on a 1y window at -111bp (0.2nd percentile 1y). USDCAD rose 1.10% over 5d and 1.74% over 1m to 1.401. Path: US front-end sold off into and after a priced FOMC hike; Canada yields rose less, so the cross-market spread made new 1y cheap extremes. Flow: CFTC TFF 2026-09-15 shows US 2Y asset-manager net longs at the 12.5th percentile 1y and leveraged-fund net still short duration but at the 93rd percentile of their own 1y net (not a new leveraged-short crowding); CAD futures leveraged funds remain net short CAD but at the 99th percentile 1y of net with +16426 weekly covering. Inference: the last 5d cheapening is a US-hike residual, not a Canada-specific easing impulse.

policy_path_check.rationale: Short-end US/Canada rates RV cannot be inferred from sovereign percentiles alone. The live SOFR and CORRA paths show the US hike is in the SOFR strip and 2028 terminal, while Canada still prices a shallow +29bp through year-end. That is the priced BoC assumption the 2Y spread is being asked to fade. AONIA is not the expression; it only confirms the global-tightening tape is not Australia-only.

context_build.price_decomposition: Level versus change: the cheapness is a level (CA-US 2Y -140bp, 3.8th percentile 1y / 4.3rd percentile 5y) plus a tactical 5d -15bp (z -2.17) and 1m -17bp. Tenor: 2Y is 29bp cheaper than CA-US 10Y (-111bp), so the dislocation is front-end, not a long-end term-premium story. US 2s10s is +25bp (0.2nd percentile 1y); CA 2s10s is +56bp (0.6th percentile 1y) — both curves are flat versus the past year, consistent with hiking-path flattening, not a Canada-only duration bid. Cash-to-2Y: US 2Y minus SOFR = 91bp; CA 2Y minus CORRA = 98bp — similar local term premia. The cross-market gap therefore is the policy-rate level gap (SOFR 3.85 versus CORRA 2.29 = 156bp cash, 149bp in 2s), now historically wide versus 5y, with the last 5d the marginal driver. Unknown: bill-minus-OIS and a live AU OIS vintage are irrelevant here; CA 2027 CORRA is missing.

trade.invalidation: Thesis is wrong if CORRA Dec stays near 2.58 and CA-US 2Y cheapens through the 2025-01-30 analog level of -145bp without a BoC-path reprice, or if Canada core remaining near 2% plus labor-gauge weakness (38) dominate energy pass-through and the US 2Y selloff simply continues as in early-cycle 2022 analogs. Right-thesis/wrong-timing if the 2024-12-18 analog path (-3bp 1m / -20bp 3m) repeats; then hold the 3m horizon rather than stop on noise. Saudi STS crude workaround reducing the oil-supply tail is a live softener of the energy catalyst.
trade.mispricing: Markets price a durable BoC near-2.3–2.6% path versus a US 2Y that already sits next to 2028 SOFR. That leaves CA-US 2Y at a 5y 4th-percentile level. The mispricing is the cross-market 2Y gap versus a policy-path-and-energy-normalized fair gap, not CAD spot and not an outright US duration call.
principal_risks: Fundamentals justify the gap: CA labor 38 vs US 75 and core near 2% can keep CA-US 2Y historically cheap.
US hiking analogs after +57bp 1m in US 2Y (2022-03-23, 2022-09-16) saw US 2Y keep rising, which can cheapen CA-US further if Canada does not catch up.
CORRA strip ends Dec-2026; missing 2027-28 Canada path can hide a fairly priced deeper hike cycle.
Saudi Oman STS workaround and modestly easier oil cut the energy-inflation tail.
No executable broker prices; parent may mark execution_blocked. Dealer short base in US 2Y (1st percentile) is squeeze risk on the receive-US leg.
trade.structure: Pay Canada 2Y vs receive US 2Y duration (long the CA minus US 2Y yield spread). Research/reference official yields and SOFR/CORRA paths only; no executable broker prices in the frozen packet.
trade.thesis: FACT: CA-US 2Y = -140bp (2026-09-17), 1y percentile 3.77, 5y percentile 4.31, 5d -15bp (z -2.17); CA 2Y 3.27, US 2Y 4.76; CORRA 2.29 with Dec 2.58; SOFR 3.85 with Dec 4.1975 and Aug-2028 4.6025; Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75–4.00% after >90% pricing; Canada CPI 3%/core ~2%; BoC minutes flag energy pass-through; BoJ hiked to 1.25%. INFERENCE: the 140bp gap is a lagging two-speed residual after a US-led, already-priced hike, not fair value once energy pass-through and broader tightening are the live transmission. Long CA-US 2Y (pay CA / receive US) owns convergence toward less-negative spreads, with carry from receiving 4.76 versus paying 3.27. UNKNOWN: CORRA beyond Dec-2026; executable marks; Canadian cash-bond positioning. This is not a screen-only fade of a cheap percentile: the analog at -145bp (2025-01-30) subsequently converged +25bp over 3m, and today’s policy-path/energy tape is why that convergence should start now rather than wait for US easing.
why_now: CA-US 2Y cheapened 15bp in 5d (z -2.17) after a Fed hike that was already >90% priced — known information, new residual.
18 Sep desk thesis: global tightening broadened (BoJ 1.25%, BoE 6–3 hawkish split) into an energy shock that constrains easing where growth is softer, including Canada.
BoC minutes flag energy pass-through while CORRA still prices only +29bp through December — the Canada path has not caught up.
Closest level analog (2025-01-30, -145bp after -17bp 1m) then converged +25bp over 3m; the same 1m move is in the tape now.
Empty $100m book pays 5% ACT/365 vig while flat; a positive-carry RV with a defined invalidation is the way to clear the hurdle.
